title: ATTACH cluster-pick weighting has no semantic pin — a uniform-pick regression passes the entire unit suite
detail: The diff's second headline behavior (cluster pick becomes a weighted draw) is pinned only via its exclusion predicate. The positive control restores suburb weight to 4 = city's 4 (parity), so weighted-vs-uniform is indistinguishable; spec §3.3's majority pin was never implemented. A uniform-pick mutation passes every unit test.
recommended_fix: Add a majority pin mirroring the SEED pin: two eligible estates in 4:1-weight districts, seed-averaged statistical run asserting the rich district's estate receives more attach spawns (or extract the cluster pick into a draw-level-testable proc).

title: growth_district_live_count's Terminal-only filter unpinned — routers counting toward district caps would pass the suite
detail: P2 gap: the proc's distinguishing predicate (routers must not consume district budget) is asserted nowhere. A mutation dropping the `.Terminal` check passes all 8 new pins plus existing board tests; only dublin golden byte-shifts would catch it.
recommended_fix: Pin it at draw level: place routers in a district at its terminal cap and assert growth_board_seed_draw still fails for it (or directly assert growth_district_live_count ignores a router-only topology).

title: Loader pass-3 district partition never asserted — district_tiles checks all run on hand-built fixtures that mirror the derivation
detail: P2 gap: test_map_district_assignment_partition validates fixture-built lists that re-implement the derivation. Deleting the loader's pass 3 (empty district_tiles → all board growth dead) fails no unit test; only golden byte-shifts would catch it.
recommended_fix: Extend test_map_board_load_districts_parse: after loading, assert the district_tiles lists sum to len(candidates) and each entry agrees with map_district_assign — same assertions as the partition test, on the loader product.

title: district_cap_permille exercised only at 1000 — the density-iteration surface and the max(1,·) floor's decisive branch untested
evidence:
core/growth.odin:521-523: `growth_district_cap :: proc(board: ^Map_Board, cat: ^Catalogs, d: u16) -> i32 {
	pool := i32(len(board.district_tiles[d]))
	cap_tiles := pool * cat.balance.growth_districts.district_cap_permille / 1000
	return max(1, cap_tiles)` — grep: district_cap_permille is set nowhere in growth_test.odin/map_test.odin; catalog_test only pins the 1..1000 range rows.
detail: P3 gap: the tunable's stated purpose (user iterates ~667 ≈ 1-in-9) has no behavioral test, and the floor branch (cap_tiles == 0 → 1) cannot fire at permille 1000, so a dropped max() passes the suite.
recommended_fix: One draw-level pin at permille 667: district with 4 pool tiles → cap 2 (third spawn excluded), plus a 1-tile district at 667 asserting the floor keeps one slot.

title: Fractional-anchor precision (MAP_ANCHOR_SCALE=10) unpinned — every real dublin anchor is fractional, every test anchor integral
evidence:
core/map.odin:469-470: `ax := i32(math.round(f64(b.districts[d].pos[0]) * MAP_ANCHOR_SCALE))
ay := i32(math.round(f64(b.districts[d].pos[1]) * MAP_ANCHOR_SCALE))` — map_test fixtures: `append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = "A", pos = {6, 6}})` / `{24, 6}` / `{10, 6}` / `{20, 6}` — data/maps/dublin.json: all 52 anchors fractional (sample Artane 18.7, 4.02; Ballsbridge 15.02, 18.84).
detail: P3 gap: constant scaling preserves distance order for integer anchors, so the scale-10 rounding path — the real board's only case — is never distinguishing. An integer-truncation mutation (round then compare unscaled) passes every fixture.
recommended_fix: Add one fixture anchor at {6.4, 6.0} (or 6.5) with a pool tile whose nearest-anchor winner flips between scaled and truncated math, asserted in the partition test.

title: Spec pin item 4 'demolished terminals free the budget' unimplemented — vacuous: E2 forbids terminal demolish and terminals never die
evidence:
core/growth.odin:530-531 comment: `a demolished terminal frees the budget (the estate-view precedent)` — core/topology.odin:273-274: `validate_demolish_node :: proc(...) -> Edit_Error {
...	if is_terminal(t, slot) { return .Terminal_Demolish } // E2` — the only node_alive=false write is apply_demolish_node (routers only); health never kills nodes.
detail: P3: the PR body and spec §3.4 claim a pinnable behavior no current mechanism can trigger; the guard is defensive-only. The unimplemented spec pin should be acknowledged, not claimed as verified.
recommended_fix: Reword the claim ('router demolish never frees terminal budget — terminals are permanent (E2)') or leave the spec pin explicitly deferred until a terminal-death mechanism exists.

title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
evidence: Pin audit vs the PR's 8-pin claim — all 8 exist: growth_test.odin:1007 (weighted majority, `testing.expectf(t, a > 2 * b, "4:1 city:suburb weights must bias the SEED draws`), 1050 (zero-weight band incl. single-eligible ok=false), 1084 (cap + exhaustion + 1-tile district), 1138 (board replay byte-identity); map_test.odin:382 (partition + tie-break: `testing.expect(t, map_district_assign(&eq, {15, 6}) == 0, "an equidistant tile must tie-break to the lower district index"`), 423 (step-level band exclusion), 447 (cap blocks both families), 477 (attach band exclusion + positive control). Catalog fail-fast FULL (7 new rows). P0 = 100%.
detail: P0 100% (replay pin, fail-fast rows, procedural inertness via goldens). P1 ≈ 88%: SEED weighting FULL; ATTACH weighting ~55% (exclusion/cap pinned, weighted-draw semantics unpinned — the blocker); caps ~90% (defaults pinned, non-default permille + floor unexercised); assignment ~85% (partition/tie-break pinned, loader assertion + fractional anchors missing). Overall ≈ 85% ≥ 80%.
recommended_fix: Lift to PASS: add the attach-weighting majority pin (the blocker), a loader-level district_tiles assertion, and a live-count router-exclusion pin — P1 reaches ≥95% with the three small additions.
